issue.title: Compile err “undefined reference to `SSL_get0_group_name'” when using as a sub_dir of a cmake project
issue.body:
modify the file MAVSDK-xxx/src/mavsdk/core/CMakeLists.txt:
`-P ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake/generate_embedded_xml.cmake`
change to:
`-P ${PROJECT_SOURCE_DIR}/../cmake/generate_embedded_xml.cmake`

so that this lib be used as a sub_dir of a cmake project:

```
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.15)
project(mavsdk_lib_pkg_cpp)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)

# if(CMAKE_COMPILER_IS_GNUCXX OR CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "Clang")
#   add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic)
# endif()

# add_definitions("-Wall -Wextra")

# find dependencies
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)

# config "MAVSDK" build options
set(SUPERBUILD ON CACHE BOOL "")
set(BUILD_MAVSDK_SERVER OFF CACHE BOOL "")
set(BUILD_WITH_PROTO_REFLECTION OFF CACHE BOOL "")
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON CACHE BOOL "")
# set(MAVLINK_DIALECT common CACHE STRING "") keep default
set(BUILD_TESTING OFF CACHE BOOL "")
set(BUILD_WITHOUT_CURL OFF CACHE BOOL "")

# set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "")

add_subdirectory(
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/MAVSDK-3.10.2
)

add_executable(test_MAVSDK src/test_MAVSDK.cpp)
target_include_directories(test_MAVSDK PUBLIC
  $<BUILD_INTERFACE:${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/include>
  $<INSTALL_INTERFACE:include/${PROJECT_NAME}>)
target_compile_features(test_MAVSDK PUBLIC c_std_99 cxx_std_17)  # Require C99 and C++17
target_link_libraries(
  test_MAVSDK
  ${rclcpp_TARGETS}
  mavsdk
)
...
```

comments.body:
Is this with latest MAVSDK? Because we had the issue for a while where it picks up the system openssl libs when it should be using the one from the SUPERBUILD.

This should have been fixed with https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2491... I'm puzzled.

Since you already use lines like:

```
find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
```

Is there a reason for not doing the same with MAVSDK? I.e. `find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)`?

> Since you already use lines like:
> 
> ```
> find_package(ament_cmake REQUIRED)
> find_package(rclcpp REQUIRED)
> ```
> 
> Is there a reason for not doing the same with MAVSDK? I.e. `find_package(MAVSDK REQUIRED)`?

Sure, I use the rk3588 orange pi 5 max board (aarch64, ubuntu 24.04) and there is no .deb provided..
So I need to compile it, and for convenience I using the "add_subdirectory()" way to import it to my cmake project(just run compile the proj, no need manually pre-install a bunch of things, that odd for a independent and portable project)

> Is this with latest MAVSDK? Because we had the issue for a while where it picks up the system openssl libs when it should be using the one from the SUPERBUILD.
> 
> This should have been fixed with [#2491](https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/pull/2491)... I'm puzzled.

the MAVSDK version is in here:
```
add_subdirectory(
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/MAVSDK-3.10.2
)
```
its the lastest MAVSDK-3.10.2
I try using the "libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_debian12_arm64.deb" install on my rk3588 orange pi 5 max board (aarch64, ubuntu 24.04).

> and there is no .deb provided

Note that `find_package` does not require a `.deb`. It tries to find a CMake config file. You can just build and install MAVSDK manually.

> no need manually pre-install a bunch of things, that odd for a independent and portable project

I don't see how that is odd 🤔.

This said, looking at your log output, it seems that MAVSDK builds correctly but the `system_tests_runner` fails. I would guess that this happens if mavsdk was built as a static library (`.a`), because then `system_tests_runner` will know about curl and openssl.

I see that above you try to set:

```
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON CACHE BOOL "")
# set(MAVLINK_DIALECT common CACHE STRING "") keep default
set(BUILD_TESTING OFF CACHE BOOL "")
```

But at least `BUILD_TESTING` is not disabled (otherwise it would not try to build the MAVSDK test targets) and therefore I suspect that `BUILD_SHARED_LIBS` has no effect either. Could you check that?

https://github.com/mavlink/MAVSDK/issues/2696#issuecomment-3456350838
If Im not install a `.deb`, and not `build and install MAVSDK manually`, then there is no way find the MAVSDK lib by `find_package`..
The `build` part just not work here.
The odd thing is for me to construct a independent and portable project, shall not manually pre-install a bunch of things to sys public path such as `/usr/bin`, OK?
The whole cmake config file and os and MAVSDK version all provided, you can just have a try.
This part shall work, because this similar way I used to other many places and they works:
```
set(BUILD_SHARED_LIBS ON CACHE BOOL "")
set(BUILD_TESTING OFF CACHE BOOL "")
```

> If Im not install a .deb, and not build and install MAVSDK manually, then there is no way find the MAVSDK lib by find_package..
The build part just not work here.

If you install it manually using `cmake --build build --target install` for instance, you then have to give cmake the path where it has been installed to, e.g. `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=path/where/installed`.

And if you want to install it somewhere specific there is `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=path/where/to/install`.

> > If Im not install a .deb, and not build and install MAVSDK manually, then there is no way find the MAVSDK lib by find_package..
> > The build part just not work here.
> 
> If you install it manually using `cmake --build build --target install` for instance, you then have to give cmake the path where it has been installed to, e.g. `-DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH=path/where/installed`.
> 
> And if you want to install it somewhere specific there is `-DCMAKE_INSTALL_PREFIX=path/where/to/install`.

You no need put these basic to me, I am asking other things...

Alright, sorry. Bottom line, we use and test `find_package(MAVSDK)`. Why don't you use that?

And if not, feel free to create a small reproducible example for us and I'll have a closer look.

> I try using the "libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_debian12_arm64.deb" install on my rk3588 orange pi 5 max board (aarch64, ubuntu 24.04).

This "libmavsdk-dev_3.10.2_debian12_arm64.deb" can be installed in my rk3588 orange pi 5 max board (aarch64, ubuntu 24.04).
So, by this method I can using MAVSDK for now.
But this way to build MAVSDK below is need to be test by using pure gcc env:
```
add_subdirectory(
    ${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/MAVSDK-3.10.2
)
```

> This part shall work, because this similar way I used to other many places and they works:

If it works, how do you explain that your build fails to build... the tests?

Your problem is happening here:

> Linking CXX executable system_tests_runner 

You don't need `system_tests_runner`. Just don't build it and you're good.
@Staok were you able to resolve your issue, or is there still something to look into?
I'm assuming this has been fixed, otherwise comment again.
